tools.name: find_customers
tools.description: Start a new search for potential customers of the user's business: recent public posts by people who are asking for, or want to buy, what the business sells. Only for finding new customers when the user asks for that; it does not list or rank leads the user already has. A search saves a campaign in

tools.name: get_search_status
tools.description: Progress of a customer search by its search id, and the leads it has found so far, best matches first. A search usually takes one to three minutes and leads appear while it runs; while the state is "searching", checking again shows newer results.

tools.name: get_my_leads
tools.description: The leads EvenLeads has already found for the user: the public post, where it was posted, a 0-10 match score and why it matched, best matches first, across all campaigns unless a campaign id is given. Reads existing leads only and starts no search. The user must be signed in with EvenLeads.

tools.name: draft_reply
tools.description: Write a first message for one lead, in the tone set on its campaign: either a private message to the author or a public reply under the post. Returns the text and a link that opens the right place to send it (with the text filled in where the platform allows). Nothing is sent: the user sends it them

tools.name: update_lead_status
tools.description: Mark one of the user's leads as contacted (they sent a message), not_relevant (not a fit; EvenLeads learns from it), closed, or back to new. Changes the lead in the user's EvenLeads account.

tools.name: list_my_campaigns
tools.description: The user's EvenLeads campaigns (id, name, status, what each one looks for). A campaign is one saved customer search. The user must be signed in with EvenLeads.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: What the signed-in EvenLeads account can still do in this period: searches, campaigns, reply drafts and stored leads left. Use it when the user asks about their plan or limits, or after a tool says something is not included.

tools.name: find_hiring_requests
tools.description: Search recent public posts where someone asks to hire a freelancer or agency for a service (web design, development, Shopify, WordPress, SEO, ads, video, copywriting, design, social media, virtual assistants and more). Returns the niche, request type, budget if stated, platform, community and age; p

tools.name: list_niches
tools.description: List the freelance and agency service niches EvenLeads tracks for hiring requests, with how many requests each had in the last 24 hours and 7 days.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search recent public hiring requests for a freelance or agency service. Returns ids, titles and links; the details of one request are available by its id.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Details of one public hiring request by its id: request type, budget, platform, community and age.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_customers, get_my_leads, find_hiring_requests · Private data: draft_reply · Public sink: get_my_leads, draft_reply, find_hiring_requests.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_customers, get_my_leads, find_hiring_requests · Private data: draft_reply · Public sink: get_my_leads, draft_reply, find_hiring_requests

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
